subject: business-studies
title: Pricing the Product Adventure
welcome_lead: How do businesses pick a price? It's smarter than you think. 🏷️
meta_desc: Goods & Services Adventure 3 — KS3 Business Studies on simple pricing strategies.
final_note: You met four pricing strategies and learned why each is used.

concepts.def: Add a profit margin to the cost
Start high then drop the price
Charge a high price for a luxury feel
Profit as a percentage of price

walkthroughs.body_html:
Cost-plus — work out the cost, add a margin.

Cost £4 + 50% margin = price £6.

Competitive — match what rivals charge. Common in supermarkets. 🛒

Skimming — start high for fans, drop later. Apple does this with new iPhones. 📱

Penetration — start low to grab market share. Many new streaming services do this.

Premium means staying high forever — like Rolex or Ferrari.

It works only with a strong brand and a USP. The high price is part of the appeal. 💎

mcqs.q: What is a brand in marketing?
options: A combination of name, design, symbols and associations that distinguishes a product and creates customer perception and loyalty — more than just a logo.
Break-even is where the business owes no debt.
A brand is the company that makes a product.
A brand is just the logo on a product.
Share prices are set by the government each morning.
The level of output where total revenue equals total costs — neither profit nor loss. It is NOT the level where profit is maximised; profit grows beyond break-even.
Break-even is where the business owes no debt.
Break-even is where the business makes the most profit.

mcqs.q: Why does a company's share price change?
options: Share prices are set by the government each morning.
A brand is the company that makes a product.
Share prices go up when a company makes more money this year.
Share prices reflect investors' expectations about future profits — driven by company performance, sector trends, economic conditions, and market sentiment.
